Compare the fits of two fit sources

Source: R/fit_sources.R
compare_fit_sources.Rd

Pairs every fit of other (e.g. the curves PRISM delivered, added by gDRcore::add_PRISM_metrics()) with the fit of reference in the same cell of the Metrics assay, and summarizes how close they are. A cell can hold several fits of other (PRISM fits one curve per pool and compound plate); each one is paired with the single reference fit of the cell.

Usage

compare_fit_sources(
  se,
  other,
  reference = "gDR",
  normalization_type = "RV",
  params = c("auc", "ec50", "x_inf"),
  metrics_assay = "Metrics",
  averaged_assay = "Averaged"
)

Arguments

se

SummarizedExperiment with a Metrics assay holding both fit sources.

other

Character string, the fit source compared with reference.

reference

Character string, the fit source it is compared with.

normalization_type

Character string, the normalization type of the fits.

params

Character vector, the parameters compared: "auc" or columns of the Metrics assay.

metrics_assay

Character string, name of the assay with the fits.

averaged_assay

Character string, name of the assay giving the concentration range of each cell.

Value

A list with pairs, a data.table with one row per fit of other: the drug, cell line and Duration, the columns that tell fits of one cell apart, and every parameter of both sources (<param>_<source>), and ec50_in_range; and summary, a data.table with one row per parameter: the number of pairs, the Spearman correlation, and the median and 95th percentile of the absolute difference; and n_unpaired, the number of fits of other in a cell with no reference fit, which are not in pairs.

Details

Two sources can describe the same curve with different parameters (gDR fixes x_0 at 1 for relative viability and gives a flat curve ec50 = 0), so the curves are compared by auc: computed from the parameters of each fit as PRISM defines AUC, the mean of the curve, clamped between 0 and 1, over log10 concentration between the lowest and highest concentration of the cell in averaged_assay. The parameters of the curve shape (ec50, x_inf, x_0, h) are compared only for pairs where both fits have their ec50 within that range (ec50_in_range), where the data define them; ec50 is compared on the log10 scale. A pair counts for a parameter only when both values are finite, so failed fits are left out of its summary.

Examples

mae <- gDRutils::get_synthetic_data("finalMAE_small")
se <- mae[[gDRutils::get_supported_experiments("sa")]]
# a copy of the gDR fits under another fit source
metrics <- gDRutils::convert_se_assay_to_dt(se, "Metrics", include_metadata = FALSE)
#> Loading required namespace: BumpyMatrix
metrics$fit_source <- "copy"
se <- gDRutils::persist_fit_assay(se, metrics, merge = "merge", assay_name = "Metrics",
                                  row = "rId", col = "cId",
                                  upsert_key_cols = c("fit_source", "normalization_type"))
compare_fit_sources(se, other = "copy")$summary
#>      parameter n_pairs spearman median_abs_diff p95_abs_diff
#>         <char>   <int>    <num>           <num>        <num>
#> 1:         auc     100        1               0            0
#> 2: log10(ec50)      98        1               0            0
#> 3:       x_inf      98        1               0            0
